steps.text:
These games can be played anytime during Book 1 (at the end of a lesson, or instead of a lesson if a student is tired). All games reinforce phonemic awareness skills using the picture cards provided with the program.

CRITICAL: DO NOT USE LETTERS. Your student should be focused on listening to sounds, not worried about which letters make those sounds.
This is a good way to teach your student the names for the pictures. It is also good practice for breaking off the first sound.
Shuffle the picture cards.
I'm going to show you a card. I want you to say the word, then say just the first sound.
Have the student make a pile for each first sound. If the first sound matches the top of an existing pile, they place it there. Otherwise, they start a new pile.
Variation: If your student is in or beyond Lesson 3, you can vary this game by sorting into piles based on the LAST sound in the word.
Pick two cards that start with the same first sound. Build a deck of 14 to 24 cards (depending on your student) and shuffle them. Lay the cards out in rows and columns face down.
We are going to play Concentration. On your turn, turn over one card, say the name of the picture, and then say just the first sound.
The player turns over a second card, says the name of the picture, and its first sound.
If the first sounds match, the person gets to keep the cards. (Optional: if the person finds a match, it is still their turn.) Person with the most cards at the end wins.
Pick four cards that start with the same first sound. You can have up to 40 cards in one game. Shuffle the cards. Deal 5 to each player. Put the rest in a draw pile.
We are going to play Go Fish. Look at your hand, pick a card, figure out its first sound, and ask me: 'Do you have a card that starts with [sound]?'

If the opponent has a card that starts with that sound, they must give it to the player. The player puts down the match. If the opponent does NOT have a match, they say 'Go Fish' and the player draws from the deck. Whoever has the most matching cards at the end wins.
Let your student choose a Bingo card. You choose a different Bingo card. Shuffle the picture cards and turn them upside down to create a draw pile. Use blank tiles as chips.
Take turns drawing a picture card. The person who draws a card must say the name of the picture, then its first sound.
Both players look at their card. If they find a picture that starts with the same sound, they cover it up with a chip.
The first person who gets 3 across, 3 down, or 3 diagonally wins. Variation: You must get a blackout to win.
Make a trail out of face-up picture cards. Make sure each picture starts with a different sound. Shuffle the rest of the cards and place them face down in a Draw pile.
Each player picks a colored tile to be their piece. Put the pieces at the beginning of the trail.
First player draws a card, says the word, and makes the first sound. Their piece advances to the picture on the trail that starts with the same sound. Then it is the other player's turn.
Optional: Allow a player's piece to go backwards if they draw a sound that is only behind them on the trail. Whoever lands on the last card in the trail wins.
Lay out four pictures in a row. Three should start with the same sound, while one starts with a different sound.
Look at these four pictures. Three start with the same sound, but one does not. Which one doesn't match?
The student must figure out and prove which picture doesn't match. Then switch places and let the student pick four cards for you to solve.
Let's play a guessing game. I am thinking of something in this room that starts with /sound/.
The student asks yes/no questions (e.g. 'Is it the XXX?'). You can set a rule that after 3 questions, you give a clue. Then reverse roles.
Variation: Don't limit it to the room. ('I am thinking of a food that starts with /b/'). You can also add syllable counting ('starts with /b/ and has 3 syllables').
Open a magazine to a page with a photograph.
Can you find two things in this picture that start with /sound/?

Then let your student ask you a similar question. 

Activity Extension (Letter Scrapbook): Have your student cut out items from pictures in a magazine. They should paste all of those that start with the same first sound on the same page of a scrapbook.
